summary: Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist. He earned a BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1992–1996) and a doctorate at Leiden University (1997–2005) under Alexander Lubotsky, also studying under Saul Migron. He held a post at Hebrew University (attested 1995–1998).
Daniel Borengasser specializes in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (1996) under Victor H. Mair, also studying under Gregory Schopen and Ludo Rocher. He serves at Cornell University.

Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied physics at Yale University (BA 1963) and regional Soviet studies at Harvard University (Master's 1965, degree 1972). In 1972, he took up a post at the University of Washington.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1980–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teachers. He held posts at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2021).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1982–2015) and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III (~1993–2015).
Daniel Franz Schauffelberger was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the University of Halle, and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1843–1845).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned an AB (~1932–1936) and AM (~1936–1938) at Harvard University, studying under Walter Eugene Clark and traditional teacher Kalipada Tarkacharya. He held a post at Harvard from 1938 to 1983.

Daniel John Gogerly was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1834), served as General Superintendent of the Wesleyan Mission in South Ceylon (1838), and held leadership posts at the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer studied at Westmar, Evangelical Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn, Mircea Eliade, and Joseph M. Kitagawa. A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, he was professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who studied at the University of Chicago (1967) and completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1965–1974). He held posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), University of Washington (1980–1995), and UCLA (1995–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at UC Berkeley, mentored by Alexander von Rospatt, alongside science degrees from Pacific Union College and UC Riverside. He held posts at the University of South Carolina and University of Hamburg.
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1980 to 2018.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was a French archaeologist and historian. He earned degrees at the University of Strasbourg and the University of Paris, studying under Henri Seyrig. He held posts at the Service des Antiquités du Haut-Commissariat au Levant (1929–1940) and Strasbourg (1955).

Daniel Sperber is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Kol Torah, Yeshivah of Flatbush, Kilburn Grammar School, and University College London (~1965–1968). He held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia (BA, MA 1987) and earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (2000). He taught at Southern Mississippi (2000–2022).

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania and studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

Daniel Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, and studied under Samli Mulkæo and Nalini Devdas. He held posts at Chiang Mai University (1999) and California State University, Chico (from 2003).
